chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is in Basra while he is from the people of Kufa, having a house and residence there. He passes through Kufa, but he is merely passing through and does not intend to stay except for the time it takes to prepare for departure, one day or two days. He (the Imam) said: 'He prays the shortened prayer (qasr) in the side of the city (when passing through). I said: 'And if he enters to visit his family?' He said: 'The full prayer (tamam) is upon him.'

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: The full prayer (performing all four rak'ahs)
key_terms.الْمِصْرِ: The city (specifically referring to Kufa in this context)

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their prayer versus offering full prayer if they have a home in the city they are passing through?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between a transient traveler and a resident by using the duration of stay in one's city of origin as the criterion for prayer length. It establishes that a brief stopover for logistical purposes does not constitute residency, thus permitting *qasr*, whereas visiting family implies a settled status requiring *tamam*. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that intention (*niyyah*) and the nature of the stay determine the legal status of the traveler.
